title: rwb-access rule-version approval: the registry's approve contract is not in the story's dependency list
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case = P7, ASM-A6-tables-3; api POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve = P7, ASM-A6-api-3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T-A.2 API-P4-017 and T6.3; _work/msr/wp/B-P4-04.md metadata for RWB-P4-AD012-APP
section: RWB-P4-AD012-APP sections 1, 3, 12.2, 12.8, 13; RWB-P4-AD012-CON sections 3, 12.2, 12.8
description: The version, its checklist and its state change are P7 rwb-decision's under the R-PREC default ruling, and the ownership map puts the rule tables and the rule-package-version approve path there. The metadata of RWB-P4-AD012-APP carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON as a contract dependency and its build list carries no P7 rule-package contract, so the two registry operations the gate calls - the approve and the version list that returns the version row with its change_checklist - have no published contract and no fake in the dependency list.
evidence: ownership.json: rule_package_version owner P7 with ruling 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision (R-PREC default ruling; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools design slide 15)' and asm ASM-A6-tables-3; api 'POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve' owner P7 with ruling and asm ASM-A6-api-3; WP B-P4-04 story row RWB-P4-AD012-APP H list ends at RWB-P4-AD011-APP and its C list is RWB-P3-E1042-CON only; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 makes the checklist, the checksum and the author and approver the registry's columns
area: rwb-access build dependency set and rule registry contract
proposed: Add the P7 rule-package contract to the contract-dependency list of RWB-P4-AD012-APP at D1, fix the two consumed operations with the P7 owner, and build the gate against that contract and its fake until it is published.

title: rwb-access rule-version approval: no rwb-access path is declared for the approval gate
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (rule-package paths x-module P3, /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve x-module P4); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rulings ASM-A6-api-3 and ASM-A6-api-4; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-012 Endpoints)
section: RWB-P4-AD012-APP section 1 Story; section 12.1 REST operations provided; RWB-P4-AD012-CON section 3 Preconditions, section 7 AC1, section 12.1
description: The legacy story approves a rule version on one path under the single monolith base, which DP-13 replaces. The technical specification carries the approval as API-P4-017 in the P4 appendix, the API Specification v4 files the same path under the rule-package group with x-module P3, the ownership map rules it P7 rwb-decision's, and no source names a rwb-access path that a console would call for the gate. The two provided paths of this story are therefore a proposal, and the sources do not say which service the SCR-39 approval control calls.
evidence: API Specification v4 line-level paths: /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve with x-module P3; /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions with x-module P3; no /admin/rule-version-approvals path anywhere in the document; ownership.json api ruling on POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve: 'the owner is P7' (ASM-A6-api-3); legacy RWB-AD-012 Endpoints table names one approve path and one list path only
proposed: Freeze the gate as two console operations under /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/rule-version-approvals with the P7 approve called as a consumed operation, and reconcile the console path with the API Specification at contract review before the document is baselined.

title: rwb-access rule-version approval: the change checklist content, its evidence and its catalogue are not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T3.1 DF-REF-295 and T6.3; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.18.3.1 BR-P4-018
section: RWB-P4-AD012-APP sections 1, 3, 4 steps 9 and 10, 8 BR6 and BR7, 11, 13; RWB-P4-AD012-CON section 8 BR9, section 11, section 13 consumer sign-off
description: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 names the seven checklist items - request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify and rollback plan - and places them in rule_package_version.change_checklist (DF-REF-295, jsonb), and says the version cannot be approved while an item is missing. No source gives the JSON shape of the column, what evidence each item must carry, how a refused item is named in a message, or the parameter key that would hold the seven item codes with their labels and required flags if the catalogue is versioned reference data, which FSD P4 A2.18 BR-P4-018 requires for a value a business person may change.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 row change_checklist: 'The seven items: request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify and rollback plan. The version cannot be approved while an item is missing | rule_package_version.change_checklist (DF-REF-295); MSG-P3-022'; T3.1 DF-REF-295 is jsonb with no structure; FSD P4 v3 A2.18.3.1 BR-P4-018 'No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version'; no FSD or TSD row defines the checklist items or the parameter key
proposed: Fix the checklist as a jsonb object with one key per item code, each carrying a present flag and a free-text evidence reference, add the seven item codes with their labels and required flags to the parameter catalogue of rwb-case, and name the missing item codes in the 409 body.

title: rwb-access rule-version approval: MSG-P3-022 is a P3 message whose text no source gives
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.3; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4.md AC-EXC-P3-016-01 and AC-EXC-P3-016-02; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-012 Validation and messages)
section: RWB-P4-AD012-APP sections 5 X5, 8 BR6, 14; RWB-P4-AD012-CON sections 5 X4, 14
description: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 cites MSG-P3-022 for an approval refused while a checklist item is missing, and the FSD P3 exception flows use the same id for a missing rollback plan and for a failed test result, but no source document in the extract set gives the message text, and the legacy RWB-AD-012 message table does not list it. The refusal is therefore declared with an id of another module's catalogue and no words, while every other message of this story has its text in the legacy story.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 cites MSG-P3-022 only; FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-016-01 'the approval is refused with MSG-P3-022 naming rollback plan'; FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-016-02 uses the same id for a failed test result; the legacy RWB-AD-012 Validation and messages table carries MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-004, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 and no MSG-P3-022
proposed: Keep MSG-P3-022 word for word from the P3 message catalogue once its text is confirmed, add it to the P4 catalogue rather than renumbering the refusal, and name the missing checklist item codes in the 409 body so the console can render the refusal from the contract.

title: rwb-access rule-version approval: the decision code and the entry fields of an approval record are not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.3; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 28; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03
section: RWB-P4-AD012-APP sections 4 step 11, 8 BR8, BR13 and BR14, 11, 13; RWB-P4-AD012-CON section 8 BR8, section 11, section 12.3
description: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 says a load, an approval and a rollback each write a change log entry with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time, and DP-03 carries the decision log to the local decision-record library and the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1. No source gives the decision code of a rule-version approval or refusal, the name of the outcome field, or whether the entry is written before or after the registry's state change; legacy test case TC-AD-012-04 only requires that a failed write stops the action.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 'A load, an approval and a rollback each write a change log entry with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time. The entry is append only'; Architecture v5 slide 28 (each service writes its record in its own schema in the same transaction as the state change, rwb-decision collects it within five minutes); DP-03 (local decision-record library and topic rwb.decision-record.v1, H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON); the only decision code named in the extract set is AC-VERS, and it belongs to the reference-load approval of RWB-AD-010
proposed: Write one entry with a decision code taken from the decision-code list of the DP-03 library, carrying the package, the version label, the status change LOADED to APPROVED or refused, the valid-from date, the approver reference and the outcome REQUESTED, in the local transaction that stores the answer and before the registry call.

title: rwb-access rule-version approval contract: the checklist state and the decision-record reference have no source definition
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.3 and T-A.2 API-P4-017; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml components RulePackageVersion; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-012 Acceptance criteria and Test cases)
section: RWB-P4-AD012-CON sections 7 AC2, 8 BR8, 11, 12.1, 12.8; RWB-P4-AD012-APP sections 12.1, 15
description: The gate's answer has to carry the checklist state and the reference of the decision-record entry it wrote, so that the console can show an approval that is recorded and the approver can see which record names it. The registry's RulePackageVersion carries the checklist as a jsonb column, the DP-03 library carries an entry with a hash and a chain sequence, and no source names the properties of the access-side answer, the field-level names of the checklist state, or the state value of a record that is written but whose downstream call timed out.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 places the checklist in rule_package_version.change_checklist (DF-REF-295, jsonb); API Specification v4 components RulePackageVersion declares the registry's shape and no access-side approval shape; T-A.2 API-P4-017 answers RulePackageVersion only; the legacy RWB-AD-012 criteria name the valid-from date and the version kept by a decided case and no record reference
proposed: Declare RuleVersionApproval with versionId, packageCode, versionLabel, validFrom, checklistState, decisionRecordReference, decisionRecordState, state, approverReference, approvedAt and the effective-dating statement, ChecklistItem per item code, and DecisionRecordRef with the entry id, the chain sequence and the outcome.

title: rwb-access rule-version approval contract: the version row is read through the package version list, whose change_checklist property is not declared
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T-A.2 API-P4-016 and API-P4-017; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rulings ASM-A6-api-3
section: RWB-P4-AD012-CON sections 7 AC4, 11, 12.2, 12.8; RWB-P4-AD012-APP sections 4 step 6, 12.2
description: The gate needs the version row - its author reference, its status, its valid-from date and its checklist - before it can decide anything, and the only registry read that returns version rows by package is the version list of API-P4-016. That operation's declared response is RulePackageVersion[] with status, checksum, author, approver, test result and dry-run counts, and the API Specification v4 does not say that change_checklist comes back with it, nor whether a version can be read by version id alone.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 API-P4-016 purpose 'List the versions of one package with status, checksum, author, approver, test result and dry run counts' with no checklist field; API Specification v4 has no GET path for a single rule-package-version except /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 places the checklist on the same row that API-P4-016 returns
proposed: Declare the version list read as consumed with the change_checklist property on each version, and if the registry publishes a single-version read instead, swap the client and the fake at contract review without changing the gate.

title: The DoA load and approval paths are not in an approved source, and two P4 stories declare them
source: Legacy RWB-AD-016 Endpoints table (POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve with Rules and parameters A; POST /admin/reference-loads with Reference data C); TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A API-P4-005 and API-P4-006; Ownership Map v1 api rows for the generic reference-load paths (owner P3, ASM-A6-api-4); RWB-P4-E1038-APP sections 12.1 and 19
section: 1 Story; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story approves the delegation of authority through the rule-version approve path and loads it through the generic reference-load path, both under the single monolith base. TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A gives the generic reference-load paths to P4 with the Reference data right, and the ownership map rules them P3 rwb-case's because the reference store is P3's. No source therefore gives a DoA-specific load or approval path. Separately, RWB-P4-E1038-APP (wave 1) already declares POST /admin/doa-loads and POST /admin/doa-loads/{loadId}/approve for the table, and this story (wave 4) serves the same two operations as the legacy load-and-approve journey, so one path is claimed by two stories with no ruling on how the work divides.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-016 Endpoints table; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006 and T-A.2; Ownership Map v1 api block for POST /admin/reference-loads (owner P3, asm ASM-A6-api-4); RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 12.1 (the four doa paths) and section 19; FSD P4 v3 A2.6
proposed: RWB-P4-E1038-APP keeps the table, its migration, the version window, the difference report, the rollback and the version read, and introduces the four paths; RWB-P4-AD016-APP builds the legacy load-and-approve journey and the lookup on those paths after it, with one controller and one owner per path. The generic reference-load and rule-version paths stay P3's and P7's and are not reused for the DoA table.

title: The delegation of authority file format is not specified
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01 (file DOA-2026.11, 95 limits, 218 stored rows); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (the delegation_limit field list); legacy RWB-AD-016 Data table
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 2 and step 4; 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Every source names the delegation workbook, its version label and its row counts, and none specifies the file: no source gives the sheet names, the column order, the unit of the amounts, how 'No limit' or 'up to X percent' is written, or whether the file carries the version label or the caller supplies it. The loader therefore cannot be written against a specified format.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026, DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062); legacy RWB-AD-016 Data table (delegation_limit, DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026)
proposed: Fix the load file as one row per limit in the column order of TSD P4 v3 T3.1, with amounts in baht to two decimals, an empty value for no limit, a percentage for a loss or price limit, and the version label carried in the file and checked against the request; the reference data administrator confirms the layout and the sample file at the data review.

title: The regulation item list is not enumerated in any source
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 (items 2.1.1, 2.1.5 and 2.1.10 in the criteria); legacy RWB-AD-016; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-056 (regulation_item varchar(10))
section: 4 Flow step 4; 7 Acceptance criteria AC4; 8 Business rules BR1
description: The criteria and the field list use regulation items such as 2.1.1, 2.1.5 and 2.1.10, and no source holds the list of items, their titles or the decisions that belong to each. The loader can check that an item is present on every row and that no row repeats a tuple, but it cannot check an item against a list of permitted items, and a test cannot prove that the item set of a version is complete.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01, AC-ALT-P4-006-01, AC-ALT-P4-006-02, AC-EXC-P4-006-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-056; legacy RWB-AD-016 Data table
proposed: Treat the regulation item as free text of up to ten characters that must be present on every row, checked for the repeated tuple and not against a list, and add the item list to the reference data of rwb-case when Risk publishes it; the values in the FSD criteria stay word for word.

title: The right that gates the approval is stated as Reference data A in one source and as Rules and parameters A in another, and as a parameter in a third
source: Legacy RWB-AD-016 Permission checks (Rules and parameters A: RW-RISK; Reference data C: RW-COE, RW-REFADM) and Endpoints (approve with Rules and parameters A); TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-006 (Reference data, right A); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-RISK RA in Rules and parameters; RW-REFADM CRUD and RW-COE CRUD in Reference data; no role with A in Reference data); FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-02 (RW-PRODHEAD refused 403 MSG-P4-002); RWB-P4-E1038-APP step 7 (the approver role is the parameter rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit)
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules BR3 and BR4; 10 Authority; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story gives the approval to the A letter in Rules and parameters and the load to the C letter in Reference data. The TSD appendix declares the generic approve path with right A in Reference data, and the TSD matrix gives no person the A letter in Reference data at all. RWB-P4-E1038-APP checks the approver against a parameter instead of a letter. Three sources, three mechanisms, one control.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-016 Permission checks and Endpoints tables; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-006 and T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-02; RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 4 step 7 and section 12.1
proposed: Read the A letter in Rules and parameters from the permission rows as the authority of the approval, keep the approver-role parameter of DP-06 as the service-level default read with the version in force so the two agree in SIT, and correct the TSD appendix declaration to right A in Rules and parameters for the DoA approval in the change register.

title: MSG-P1-002 and MSG-P7-010 are messages of other catalogues and the P4 message list does not carry them
source: Legacy RWB-AD-016 Validation and messages table (MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P7-003); FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-01 and AC-EXC-P4-006-04; RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 14
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC4 and AC9; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy criteria refuse a file with MSG-P1-002 and answer a missing limit with MSG-P7-010, both messages of other modules' catalogues, and the P4 message list of the same legacy story carries neither. No source says whether the P4 service reuses the two ids or takes ids of its own.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-016 Validation and messages table; FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-01 and AC-EXC-P4-006-04; RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 14 (MSG-P1-002 and MSG-P7-010 texts)
proposed: Keep MSG-P1-002 and MSG-P7-010 word for word and add both to the P4 catalogue as shared entries, because the legacy criterion and the FSD use those ids; one rule keeps one message id in the loader and in the decision centre.

title: Who raises the incident behind a NOT_COVERED answer is not specified
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-04 (the lookup returns NOT_COVERED and an incident is raised to the RW-RISK queue with MSG-P7-010); legacy RWB-AD-016 AC2; RWB-P4-E1038-APP exception path X6 (rwb-decision raises the incident)
section: 4 Flow step 12; 5 Exception paths X10; 7 Acceptance criteria AC9; 14 Validation and messages
description: The FSD says the lookup returns NOT_COVERED and that an incident is raised to the RW-RISK queue with MSG-P7-010. MSG-P7-010 is a decision-centre message and the incident queue is not the access service's, and no source says whether the lookup call itself raises the incident, or the calling router does, or rwb-decision does on the routing request. The answer shape therefore cannot be fixed without a ruling on the owner of the incident.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-04; legacy RWB-AD-016 AC2; RWB-P4-E1038-APP exception path X6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-decision owns approvals and the central ledger)
proposed: The lookup answers NOT_COVERED with MSG-P7-010 naming the decision and the product and an incidentReference to the RW-RISK queue; the incident record itself is raised on the routing side by rwb-decision, which owns MSG-P7-010 and the approval record, and this service produces the answer and the reference only.

title: The RELATED_PARTY answer does not say whether the reason is a code on the answer or a row condition
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-05 (the lookup returns level L1 with reason RELATED_PARTY); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-057 (applies_when); RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 8 BR5 and section 13 (the item 2.1.10 rows with WO_CRITERIA_MET and WO_CRITERIA_NOT_MET)
section: 4 Flow step 12; 7 Acceptance criteria AC10; 8 Business rules BR10; 12.1 REST operations provided
description: The FSD states that a write-off for a related party answers L1 with reason RELATED_PARTY. The table holds an applies_when column and the write-off item 2.1.10 is loaded as two condition rows, so the answer could carry the reason as a code returned to the caller or as the row's own condition text. No source fixes which, and a consumer needs to know whether to read a reason field at all.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-057; RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 8 BR5 and section 13
proposed: Return approvalLevel L1 with reason RELATED_PARTY as a coded value on the answer, read from the row whose applies_when condition is the related-party one, and keep the condition text in the row only; the reason code is a value of a reference list so a new reason needs no build.

title: The field-level schema of the load, approval and lookup answers is not specified
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01 and AC-ALT-P4-006-01; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A; legacy RWB-AD-016 Data table
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided
description: The sources name the facts an answer must carry and none fixes the field-level schema: no string lengths, no date or timestamp format, no shape or member count of the difference report, no maximum length of the incident reference, and no page or size for a version list. A consumer can build against the field names only.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A; legacy RWB-AD-016 Data table and Endpoints table
proposed: Fix the field names of section 11 in the OpenAPI 3.1 document with dates as ISO 8601 dates, amounts as decimal strings of two decimals, LOV codes as their value codes and an incident reference of up to forty characters, and leave lengths and the difference report members to the contract review.

title: The DoaLimitChanged event key and payload are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged) and slide 43 (consumers: all, cache refresh); RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 12.3
section: 4 Flow step 11; 12.3 Events published; 12.8 Contract fakes; 14 Validation and messages
description: Architecture v5 names the event, its topic and its consumers, and gives no key and no payload. RWB-P4-E1038-APP proposes key limitVersion with a payload of version, table, change kind and two dates; no source confirms it, and a consumer that caches the table needs the key and the payload fixed before it can subscribe.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 and slide 43; RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 12.3
proposed: Publish rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 on rwb.access.events.v1 keyed on limitVersion, with limitVersion, table, change kind, validFrom, validTo and rowCount, in a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with no personal data, through the outbox after the commit; the cache-refresh consumers confirm the payload at contract review.

title: The lookup operation is claimed by two P4 stories
source: Ownership Map v1 api row GET /doa-limits (owner P4); RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 1 and section 19 (the lookup is RWB-P4-E2013-APP's, legacy RWB-E2-013); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-decision calls REST Access: DoA limits)
section: 1 Story; 12.1 REST operations provided; 19 Out of scope
description: The ownership map gives GET /doa-limits to P4, and both stories of the service claim it: RWB-P4-E1038-APP states that the lookup belongs to RWB-P4-E2013-APP (approval routing, legacy RWB-E2-013, wave 2), and the legacy RWB-AD-016 criterion AC2 requires the lookup answer as part of this key. No source divides the answer from the routing, so one path could be served twice with two shapes.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api block GET /doa-limits (owner P4, basis Architecture v5 slide 41 and TSD P4 v3 T3.1); RWB-P4-E1038-APP section 1 and section 19; RWB-P4-E2013-APP in the split plan (legacy RWB-E2-013); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14
proposed: The lookup operation is served once by rwb-access, on the ownership map's path; RWB-P4-AD016-APP owns the answer over the DoA table, because legacy AC2 requires it, and RWB-P4-E2013-APP owns the routing that consumes the answer and holds no second copy of the path; the division is confirmed at contract review.

title: The HTTP status of a NOT_COVERED answer is not specified
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-04; legacy RWB-AD-016 AC2; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A (no lookup endpoint)
section: 5 Exception paths X10; 12.1 REST operations provided; 14 Validation and messages
description: The FSD says the lookup returns NOT_COVERED and that an incident follows. No source says whether the answer is a success with a status field, a 404, or a 409, and a consumer that treats it as an error would fail a request that is a legitimate business answer. The legacy criteria are silent because the answer did not cross a service boundary.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 AC-EXC-P4-006-04; legacy RWB-AD-016 AC2; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A
proposed: Answer 200 with status NOT_COVERED, the message id MSG-P7-010, the decision and the product in the detail, and an incidentReference, so a router can hold the item and tell Risk without treating a legitimate answer as a transport error.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: the rule arm calls the P7 rule-package rollback, but the story's contract-dependency list carries only P3 contracts
source: Ownership Map v1 (api POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback = P7, ruling ASM-A6-api-3; table rule_package_version = P7, ruling ASM-A6-tables-3); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-018; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 notes; WP B-P4-04 metadata for RWB-P4-AD013-APP
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 12.2 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Build step 6
description: The rule half of the legacy rollback - withdrawing a rule package version and putting the version before it in force - is rwb-decision's (P7) under the R-PREC default ruling, and the ownership map puts the four rule-package paths there. The metadata of RWB-P4-AD013-APP carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON as contract dependencies, so the rule-package rollback the gate calls has no published contract and no fake in the dependency list, while the reference arm's P3 contract is named. The legacy story also presents both restores as one action on one screen, which is the split this story records.
evidence: Ownership map ruling on rule_package_version: 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision (R-PREC default ruling; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools design slide 15)'; api ruling on POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback places it with P7 (ASM-A6-api-3); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-018 is the only rollback of a rule version in the technical specification; WP B-P4-04 story JSON for RWB-P4-AD013-APP lists C = [RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON] only.
proposed: Build the rule arm against the P7 rule-package rollback contract and its fake, publish that contract with the P7 contract story of the legacy key, and add the missing C dependency to the metadata at D1.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: no rwb-access rollback path and no read-back resource exist in the API Specification v4 or the P4 technical specification
source: API Specification v4 (no /admin/version-rollbacks path, no x-module P4 rollback resource); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-010 and API-P4-018 are the owners' paths; no administration rollback of its own); legacy RWB-AD-013 endpoints
section: Section 1 Story; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.9 Call-type summary; section 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story names the monolith's rule-version load and approve paths under the single recovery base that DP-13 replaces, and it names no rollback path at all. The targets that own the two restores declare their own rollback operations (API-P4-018 for a rule package version and API-P4-010 for a reference load), and the API Specification v4 declares no rwb-access rollback path. Neither source declares a rollback resource that can be read back after the call, so both provided operations and the rollbackId the answer returns are the story's own.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013 endpoints table: POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-010 'Roll back an approved reference data version to the version before it' and API-P4-018 'Roll back a package version in force to the version before it, with a reason'; no T-A entry for an administration rollback path; ownership map carries no /admin/version-rollbacks entry.
proposed: Provide POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/version-rollbacks and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/version-rollbacks/{rollbackId}, serve the read from the stored answer of the accepted call and its two decision-record entries, and confirm the two paths with the console and both owners at contract review.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: one legacy action covers a rule version and a reference-data version whose restores belong to two owners, and no source defines a request that carries the target kind
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 story and AC1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.22 (FEAT-ADM-06, 'returns any versioned table to its previous version'); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-010 and API-P4-018 (two different requests and rights)
section: Section 1 Story; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 3; section 8 Business rules BR1; section 12.1 Contract
description: The legacy criterion says the previous version is loaded through the same load, whatever the version is, because the monolith held the rule version and the reference version in one module behind one screen. In the target the two restores are two operations with two owners, two rights and two answer shapes, and no source defines a request that names which of the two is meant. Without that field the gate cannot choose an owner, and a rule version could be sent to the reference-data path or the reverse.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013: 'As a reference data administrator, I want the previous version restored through the same load'; FSD P4 v3 A2.22: 'Returns any versioned table to its previous version and records the rollback' with role 'Platform administrator' and prerequisite FEAT-CWC-15; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-010 authorisation 'Reference data, right U' against API-P4-018 'Rules and parameters, right U'.
proposed: Carry targetKind (RULE or REFERENCE), targetId, previousVersionId, effectiveDate and reason in one request, choose the owner from targetKind alone, and confirm the two values with the console and both owners at contract review.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: the loader's right on a rule or reference version is given as C in the legacy permission checks and as U in the technical specification and API-P4-018
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 permission checks (Rules and parameters C for RW-COE, A for RW-RISK); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 ('RW-COE: C, U: upload a version, list it, dry-run it and roll back') and T-A.2 API-P4-018 ('Rules and parameters, right U')
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 4; section 8 Business rules BR4; section 12.1 Contract
description: The legacy story grants the load with the C letter and the approval with the A letter and says nothing about a rollback right. The technical specification gives RW-COE both C and U on rule packages and authorised the rollback operation with U, while the reference-load rollback is authorised with U in Reference data. A gate that demanded C would refuse the role the specification designs for the rollback, and a gate that demanded U alone would refuse the loader's own C on the reference arm.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013 permission checks: 'Rules and parameters | C | RW-COE' and 'Rules and parameters | A | RW-RISK'; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 refine table: 'RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | C, U: upload a version, list it, dry-run it and roll back'; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-018 'Authorization | Rules and parameters, right U, scope applied'; API-P4-010 'Reference data, right U'.
proposed: Read the loader's right as a set: either the C or the U letter in the capability area of the target satisfies the loader, the A letter is required of the approver, and the letters come from the permission rows and never from a role code.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: 'and the owner approves' leaves the approver's area right, the message text and the refusal status of a self-approval open
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1 and permission checks; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T6.3 (author and approver, MSG-P7-002); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.22.4.1 AC-P4-022-01 and A2.22.4.3; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-EXC-P10-001-03 (409 with MSG-P7-002)
section: Section 1 Story; section 4 Flow step 8; section 5 Exception paths X6; section 8 Business rules BR4; section 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy criterion has the owner approve a rollback but names no area right for the approver beyond the Rules and parameters A of the permission table, which covers a rule version and says nothing about a reference-data version. The technical specification refuses an author's own approval with MSG-P7-002 but carries no text for the message, and the sources disagree on the status: the P4 approval story answers 403 and the FSD P10 and P3 examples answer 409. The message text, the status and the reference-data approver right therefore each need a decision before the gate is coded.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1: 'When I load the previous version with an immediate date and the owner approves'; legacy permission checks list only Rules and parameters C and A, with no Reference data row; TSD P4 v3 T6.3: 'the author cannot approve ... MSG-P7-002' with no message text; FSD P10 v3 AC-EXC-P10-001-03: 'the approval is refused with 409 and MSG-P7-002'; RWB P4 AD010 APP answers 403 for the same condition.
proposed: Keep MSG-P7-002 verbatim from the decision centre's catalogue, answer 409 for the separation-of-duty refusal on a rollback, require the A letter of the approver in the area of the target, and confirm the text, the status and the reference-data approver right with the decision centre and Risk at contract review.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: the two decision-record entries of a rollback have no decision code and no field set in any source
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1 ('both changes are logged'); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.3 (a rollback writes a change log entry) and T3.1 DF-REF-294 rollback_of; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (decision record fields); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-39
section: Section 1 Story; section 4 Flow steps 10 and 13; section 8 Business rules BR6; section 11 Data
description: The legacy criterion says both changes are logged and the technical specification says a load, an approval and a rollback each write a change log entry, but no source says which decision codes the two facts carry, what an entry of a rollback holds, or how a reader pairs the withdrawal with the restoration. The decision record of slide 16 lists chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash and entry_hash; none of them names a rollback.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1: 'Then decisions from that time use the previous version and both changes are logged'; TSD P4 v3 T6.3: 'A load, an approval and a rollback each write a change log entry with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time'; Temporal and Drools slide 16 notes field list; no decision-code list is published in TSD P4 v3 T3.2.
proposed: Write two entries per accepted rollback with the proposed decision codes VER-WDRW (the withdrawal of the version in force) and VER-RSTR (the restoration of the previous version), each carrying the target kind, the two version labels, the effective date, the loader and approver references and the outcome, and take the final codes from the decision-code list when it is published.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: 'with an immediate date' is not defined, and no source says whether a rollback may be dated in the future or the past
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.22.2 step 2 and A2.22.3.1 VR-P4-022-1 (MSG-GEN-001); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T4 (states and effective dating) and API-P4-018
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 7; section 5 Exception paths X2; section 8 Business rules BR3
description: The legacy criterion asks for an immediate date and stops there. A rollback applied from a future date leaves the bad version in force until that date, and one applied from a past date re-decides working that has already been reported and may already have been sampled; the sources define effective dating for a new version (R-UNI-38) but say nothing about the date of a rollback. The gate's refusal of a back-dated rollback and its naming of the field are therefore the story's reading.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1: 'When I load the previous version with an immediate date and the owner approves'; FSD P4 v3 A2.22.2 step 2 'Enters or confirms the values' with VR-P4-022-1 'Required field empty | MSG-GEN-001'; TSD P4 v3 T4 gives the version lifecycle but no rollback date rule; R-UNI-38 states that a new version applies from its effective date.
proposed: Read 'an immediate date' as today's business date, refuse a date before today with MSG-GEN-001 naming effectiveDate and nothing written, and confirm with Compliance whether a future-dated rollback is ever permitted before the rule is frozen.

title: rwb-access rollback gate: the rollback reason has no length, no coded list and no required flag in either owner's RollbackRequest
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-010 and API-P4-018 (RollbackRequest, errors 422); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.9.4.3 AC-EXC-P4-009-02 (a reason of 20 to 1000 characters for break-glass); legacy RWB-AD-013
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 6; section 8 Business rules BR13; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Both owner rollback operations take a RollbackRequest and both can answer 422, but neither source says what the reason must contain, how long it may be or whether it is required. The only coded-reason discipline in the same module belongs to the break-glass request, which refuses a reason shorter than 20 or longer than 1000 characters. The gate must decide the bound before it can refuse a bad reason, and the bound must be a parameter rather than a constant.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 API-P4-010 request 'RollbackRequest', errors '401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503'; API-P4-018 request 'RollbackRequest', errors '401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503'; no field table for RollbackRequest in T-A.2; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-009-02: 'a reason of 12 characters ... refused with status 422 and message MSG-GEN-002 for field reason with min 20 and max 1000'.
proposed: Require a reason of 20 to 1000 characters, hold both bounds as parameter rows read with the version in force, carry the reason to the owner unchanged, and replace the free text with a coded list when the owners publish one.

title: rwb-access rollback contract: the two provided operations and the read of a rollback have no source path, operation id or resource to baseline against
source: API Specification v4 index (no rwb-access rollback operation); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1 endpoint inventory and T-A.2 (only API-P4-010 and API-P4-018 are rollbacks); legacy RWB-AD-013 endpoints
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.9 Call-type summary
description: A contract baseline is anchored on the published operation inventory of its service. `rwb-access` has an inventory in the API Specification and in the P4 appendix, and neither carries a rollback operation or a rollback resource; the two rollbacks in the inventory belong to `rwb-case` and `rwb-decision`. The document therefore declares two operations and a read whose paths, operation ids and tags are the contract's own, and the review has to accept them as new rather than as a restatement of a source line.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 endpoint inventory lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no administration rollback; T-A.2 API-P4-010 'POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback' and API-P4-018 'POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback' are the only rollbacks and both are consumed here; no source defines a read of a rollback by an identifier.
proposed: Baseline POST /admin/version-rollbacks and GET /admin/version-rollbacks/{rollbackId} under the service base, declare the read as served from the stored answer of the accepted call and its two record references, and record the two operations as new in the API Specification index at the next version.

title: rwb-access rollback contract: the restored version, the effective-from time, the two decision-record references and the statement about decisions from that time have no field-level definition
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (rule_package_version DF-REF-279 to DF-REF-295, rollback_of DF-REF-294) and T4; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 notes (one-call rollback); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-38
section: Section 7 Acceptance criteria AC6; section 8 Business rules BR7; section 11 Data; section 12.1 Contract; section 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy criterion states the outcome in prose: decisions from that time use the previous version, and both changes are logged. The technical specification holds the fields of a rule package version, including rollback_of, but defines no answer of a rollback and no field that names the two record entries; the reference side defines neither. A contract that cannot say what the answer's fields are cannot be faked, and a screen that rebuilds the statement itself can disagree with the record.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1: 'Then decisions from that time use the previous version and both changes are logged'; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 rule_package_version DF-REF-279 to DF-REF-295 with DF-REF-294 rollback_of and no record-reference field; TSD P4 v3 T4 describes the states but not the answer; API-P4-018 response 'RulePackageVersion' and API-P4-010 response 'ReferenceLoad' differ from each other.
proposed: Declare VersionRollback with rollbackId, targetKind, targetId, restoredVersion, effectiveFrom, state, decisionRecordRefs (exactly two) and statement, declare the statement once in the contract, and have both screens show it from the answer rather than rebuild it.

title: rwb-access rollback contract: the two decision codes of the entries have no published list, so the contract declares proposed values
source: Legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.3 and T3.2 (no decision-code list); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (decision record fields); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-39
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 8 Business rules BR4; section 11 Data; section 12.7 Tables owned
description: The contract has to declare the two entries of a rollback as contract elements, with their codes, because the answer carries two references and a reader must be able to tell which is the withdrawal and which is the restoration. No source publishes a decision-code list for an administration action: the P4 appendix lists LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE-CLASS, LOV-SCOPE and LOV-VERSION-STATUS but no LOV-DECISION, and the platform and event catalogues name events rather than codes.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3: 'A load, an approval and a rollback each write a change log entry with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time'; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 lists seven lists of values and none of them is a decision-code list; Temporal and Drools slide 16 field list has no decision code for a rollback.
proposed: Declare the two codes as proposed values VER-WDRW and VER-RSTR in the contract and in the fakes, mark them as pending the decision-code list, and re-point them when the list is published without a change of the answer shape.

title: rwb-access rollback contract: the self-approval refusal has no text in the P4 module and its status is 403 in one P4 story and 409 in the FSD examples
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.3 (MSG-P7-002, no text); RWB P4 AD010 APP (403 for a self-approval); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 AC-EXC-P10-001-03 and FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 AC-EXC-P3-006-01 (409 with MSG-P7-002); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.22.4.3 AC-EXC-P4-022-01 (MSG-P4-002 for a missing right)
section: Section 5 Exception paths X3; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC3; section 14 Validation and messages
description: The contract declares one condition-to-status mapping, and the separation of duty is the one condition whose mapping is contested: the P4 approval story answers 403 because the right is absent, and the FSD examples for an agent configuration and for a queue version answer 409 because the state forbids the action. The message id is MSG-P7-002 in all of them, but the P4 technical specification carries no message text, so a document that declares the message must take both the text and the status from another source and say so.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3: 'The author who loaded the version and the approver who approved it, with both times; the author cannot approve ... MSG-P7-002' with no text column; RWB P4 AD010 APP: 'refused 403 with MSG-P7-002'; FSD P10 v3 AC-EXC-P10-001-03: 'the approval is refused with 409 and MSG-P7-002'; FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-006-01: 'the approval is refused with MSG-P7-002 And version 4 stays VALIDATED and is not in force'.
proposed: Declare the separation-of-duty refusal once, as 409 with MSG-P7-002 in the decision centre's verbatim text, state in the contract that the status is chosen for this gate and differs from the approval gate by design, and confirm both with the decision centre owner before the baseline is tagged.

title: rwb-access queue-load gate: API Specification v4 declares no rwb-access path for the queue load, the approval or the read
source: API Specification v4 P4 administration paths API-P4-004 to API-P4-021; API Specification v4 /admin/reference-loads and /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; Ownership Map v1 api ruling on POST /admin/reference-loads (owner P3, ASM-A6-api-4); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2; WP B-P4-04 metadata and design line for RWB-P4-AD014-APP
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The gate needs three operations - the queue file load, the approval of a loaded queue version and the read of a load - and API Specification v4 declares none of them on the rwb-access base. The reference-load family it does declare is x-module P4 in name only: the ownership ruling puts POST /admin/reference-loads, its approve, verify and rollback and the list read with P3 rwb-case under ASM-A6-api-4, because the queue and the reference version are rwb-case's tables. The story therefore declares its own two console operations, and the approval rides on the same POST as a second request shape because the design line fixes two served paths.
evidence: API Specification v4 T-A.1 style inventory: API-P4-004 GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, API-P4-005 POST /admin/reference-loads, API-P4-006 POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve and the role, access-log, rule-package and smoke paths only; no queue path on the P4 base. Ownership map: POST /admin/reference-loads owner P3, ruling '... the plan Appendix R default ruling puts parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) in rwb-case, so the owner is P3' (ASM-A6-api-4). TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-005 purpose 'Load reference data: lists, queues, timers, templates, delegation limits'.
proposed: Declare POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/queue-loads with its two request shapes (multipart load, JSON approval) and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/queue-loads/{loadId} in the RWB-P4-AD014-CON document, keep the owner's reference-load family consumed, and add the two operations to the P4 API file at D1.

title: rwb-access queue load: the legacy story's endpoints row names rule-version paths that belong to RWB-AD-011 and RWB-AD-012, and depends on the monolith queue story
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md RWB-AD-014 Endpoints row and Depends on row; API Specification v4 rule-package paths API-P4-014 to API-P4-021; Ownership Map v1 api rulings on the rule-version and rule-package paths (ASM-A6-api-3); Ownership Map v1 queue, queue_member and assignment rows (P3)
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow; section 12.1 and 12.2 Contract
description: The legacy story Configure queues carries an endpoints table of GET admin rule-versions and POST admin rule-versions/{versionId}/approve, which are the rule-version read and approve of RWB-AD-011 and RWB-AD-012, and a dependency on the monolith queue story. Neither names a queue load. The target keeps the queue model and the allocation with P3 rwb-case and the rule registry with P7 rwb-decision, so the legacy endpoints row can be read neither as this story's provided surface nor as its consumed surface.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-014 Endpoints: 'GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions | Rules and parameters R' and 'POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve | Rules and parameters A'; Depends on: RWB-E1-019. Ownership map rule-version paths owner P7 with ruling ASM-A6-api-3; ownership map queue, queue_member and assignment owner P3.
proposed: Read the endpoints row as a copy of the rule-version key and replace it with this story's two operations, and read the RWB-E1-019 dependency as the queue and allocation work now owned by RWB-P3-E1019-APP and its contract RWB-P3-E1019-CON.

title: rwb-access queue load: the queue file layout is not specified, and the legacy file's member sheet is a P3 table
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.2 API-P4-005 (multipart file, table, validFrom); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.3 AC-P4-003-01 (QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER sheets, 12 queues, 48 member rows); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 queue and queue_member; Ownership Map v1 queue_member (P3)
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 5 and 6; section 8 Business rule BR2; section 12.1 Contract
description: Neither the FSD nor the technical specification states the sheet name, the header row or the column order of a queue file, and neither says whether the member rows ride in the same upload. The FSD example loads a QUEUE sheet and a QUEUE_MEMBER sheet as one version with 48 member rows, but queue_member is P3 rwb-case's table and this gate owns no member row, so the member sheet cannot be loaded here and its route is not specified either.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-003-01: 'the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER sheets are loaded as version 1 with valid from 2026-11-30 and approved ... And 48 member rows are in force'; TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-005 request 'Multipart: file, table, validFrom' with no layout; Ownership map queue_member owner P3, basis 'TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (queue_member NEW)'.
proposed: Declare the queue file as one row per queue with queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, caseload_cap, overflow_queue_code and valid_from, fix the sheet name and header order with the reference data administrator and the rwb-case owner before the parser is frozen, and route the member rows through the rwb-case reference load as its own table code.

title: rwb-access queue load: no caseload cap value and no default cap is specified
source: TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 DF-WRK-007 capacity_cap (optional); Decision Log v10 DL23; Business Requirements Program v4 DL23 row; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 AC-ALT-P4-003-02 (capacity 40, AT_CAP, overflow TDR-BKK-OVF)
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 8 Business rule BR5; section 11 Data; section 16 Test cases
description: The owner's queue field capacity_cap is optional, and DL23 says the cap and the queue order are loaded as parameters when the business supplies them. No source gives an in-force cap, a default cap for a queue row without one, or the cap at which a case is sent to the overflow queue. The gate therefore validates only that a cap present in the file is a positive integer, and the app story carries the placeholder wherever a value would be needed.
evidence: TSD P3 T3.1: 'DF-WRK-007 | capacity_cap | NUMBER | integer | No | None'; Decision Log v10 DL23: 'What is the most cases a person holds, and how is a queue ordered? | Not a choice. A value per role and a queue order from the business. | Load as parameters.'; FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-003-02 gives capacity 40 for member U-11 of queue TDR-BKK-CO as test data only.
proposed: Keep the cap out of code entirely: a row without a cap is accepted, a cap present is validated as a positive integer, and the values are supplied by the business through DL23 when they are agreed.

title: rwb-access queue load: the assignment-method list LOV-ASSIGN is declared in the P3 specification and absent from the P4 specification the gate is written from
source: TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 DF-WRK-006 (LOV-ASSIGN) and T3.2 (LOV-ASSIGN values); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 and T3.2; TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-005
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 8 Business rule BR4; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The queue row's assignment_method is a value of LOV-ASSIGN, and the list is declared only in the P3 technical specification: TSD P4 T3.2 carries LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE-CLASS, LOV-SCOPE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-ROUTE-SET, LOV-RULE-TABLE and LOV-VERSION-STATUS and no LOV-ASSIGN, while TSD P3 T3.2 carries the list with four values. The gate validates the column, so it must read the list through the reference-data contract of rwb-case and hold no value of its own; a value list written into rwb-access would be a second truth.
evidence: TSD P3 T3.1: 'DF-WRK-006 | assignment_method | LOV | varchar(20) | Yes | LOV-ASSIGN'; TSD P3 T3.2: '| LOV-ASSIGN | ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER, SKILL |'; TSD P4 T3.2 lists seven lists and none of them is LOV-ASSIGN.
proposed: Read LOV-ASSIGN through the rwb-case reference-data contract with the version in force, name the list in the contract document and declare no value of it in rwb-access; add LOV-ASSIGN to the P4 list section at D1 so the two specifications agree.

title: rwb-access queue load: the required answer carries a version label and a state the owner's load schema does not return, and the load decision code is not specified
source: API Specification v4 components.schemas.ReferenceLoad (id, table, validFrom, status, rows); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 reference_version DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-180; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.3 and API-P4-006 note on the decision log entry
section: Section 1 Story; section 8 Business rule BR14; section 11 Data; section 12.1 Contract; section 15 Screens and states
description: The load answer this story must return is the load id, the row count, the version label, validFrom and the state. The owner's ReferenceLoad schema carries id, table, validFrom, status and rows, so the version label has no field in the load answer and must come from the owner's reference-data read of the version; and the state the gate reports is the owner's status, not a state of its own. The decision code of the load entry of the decision-record library is not specified in any source, while the approve operation declares its own entry.
evidence: API Specification v4 ReferenceLoad properties: id, table, validFrom, status, rows. TSD P3 T3.1 reference_version: DF-REF-162 version_label, DF-REF-165 status, DF-REF-169 row_count, DF-REF-171 load_id. API Specification v4 API-P4-006 description: 'Approval writes a decision log entry with decision code AC-VERS.'
area: rwb-access queue load answer and audit
proposed: Declare the answer as loadId, rowCount, versionLabel, validFrom and state, take the version label from the owner's reference-data read of the version and the state from its status, and take the decision code of the load entry from the owner's approve entry code until the P3 and P7 owners name one.

title: rwb-access queue load: legacy AC1 states an allocation outcome that this story does not own
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md RWB-AD-014 AC1; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.7, A2.8 and FEAT-CWC-08; Ownership Map v1 queue, assignment and task rows (P3); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (ALLOCATION package)
section: Section 1 Story; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; section 8 Business rule BR7; section 16 Test cases TC-AD-014-01
description: The legacy criterion says that after a load and an approval allocation uses the new method and cap from the valid-from date. The allocation step, the assignment row and the cap arithmetic are P3 rwb-case's, and this story owns no allocation code, so the criterion can only be proved in this story against the owner's contract answer. The reading used here is that the rwb-case contract face returns the allocation decision naming the assignment method and the cap of the new version in force from its valid-from date, and that the end-to-end proof belongs to the integration harness.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-014 AC1: 'Given a queue file / When it is loaded and approved / Then allocation uses the new method and cap from the valid from date'; Ownership map queue, assignment and task owner P3; Temporal and Drools slide 16: the ALLOCATION table fires a queue and an owner role, with the cap applied on owner selection.
proposed: Prove AC1 in this story against the rwb-case contract mock that returns the allocation decision of the new version from its valid-from date, and prove the live allocation in RWB-ITG-AD014-ITG on the owner's placement path.

title: rwb-access queue load: the approval right is declared as Reference data A held by no role, as Rules and parameters A for RW-RISK, and as a per-table approver role
source: API Specification v4 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006 notes; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix and rule-package refinement; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md RWB-AD-014 Permission checks; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 AC-EXC-P4-003-01 and AC-EXC-P4-004-03
section: Section 1 Story; section 8 Business rule BR8; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract; section 14 Validation and messages
description: Three readings of the approval right meet in this story. The legacy permission table gives Rules and parameters A to RW-RISK and R to the case roles. The technical specification gives RW-RISK RA in Rules and parameters, RW-REFADM CRUD in Reference data and RW-COE CRUD in both areas. The API specification says of the reference-load approve that Reference data A is held by no role and that the approver role for the load's table must be checked. A queue load is a reference-data load, so the gate could check Reference data A and refuse every caller, or check Rules and parameters A and admit RW-RISK as the legacy story says.
evidence: API Specification v4 API-P4-006 description: 'Authorization: Reference data A is held by no role. Check the approver role for the load's table (see gaps) and that the caller is not the loader (409 MSG-P7-002).'; TSD P4 T6.1: 'RW-RISK Risk and model risk officer | RA | R | -' in Rules and parameters; legacy RWB-AD-014 Permission checks: 'Rules and parameters | A | RW-RISK'; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-03: a loader is refused with MSG-P7-002 and an RW-COE caller with MSG-P4-002.
proposed: Check the A letter in Rules and parameters for the approval, as the legacy story and T6.1 say, keep the four-eyes comparison on top of it, and record the Reference data A wording of the API specification as the row to correct when the P4 API file is next published.

title: rwb-access queue load contract: no source publishes the queue-row schema or the file layout the document must declare
source: WP B-P4-04 design line for RWB-P4-AD014-CON; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 DF-WRK-002 to DF-WRK-008; API Specification v4 API-P4-005 and components.schemas.ReferenceLoad; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 AC-P4-003-01
section: Section 2 Business rationale; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC2; section 11 Data; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Build steps
description: The contract baseline has to declare one row shape for the queue file and one answer shape for the load, and no source publishes either: the owner's technical specification lists the queue fields, the FSD names two sheets and the API specification names a multipart file with a table code and a date. The document therefore declares the eight columns of the design line, names the list and the optional cap without a value, and marks the sheet name, the header row and the column order as a gap so the app story and the console build against one shape.
evidence: TSD P3 T3.1 queue fields DF-WRK-002 to DF-WRK-008 with no file; API Specification v4 API-P4-005 request 'Multipart: file, table, validFrom'; ReferenceLoad carries no row schema; FSD P4 AC-P4-003-01 names a QUEUE sheet and a QUEUE_MEMBER sheet only.
proposed: Declare QueueFileRow with the eight columns, QueueLoad with the five answer fields and QueueValidationError with the row, the field and the detail, and freeze the sheet name and the header order with the P3 owner and the reference data administrator at the contract review.
